- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast to align with downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; add 1–2 days of upward bias in forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) if sentiment is bullish; add 0.5–1.5% per day to end of forecast.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model underreacts; apply 0.5–1.0% lag correction to forecast.
